podcast.title: Commercial Success at Specialty
podcast.body: Guitar Slim was among the Specialty Records artists who were achieving significant commercial success, with sales described as "hand-over-fist." "other specialty acts, like Lloyd Price, Jesse Belvin, and guitar slim, were all selling hand-over-fist."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Great Blues Guitarist and Showman
podcast.body: Guitar Slim was one of the great blues guitarists of the 1950s and an exceptional showman, famous for his performance style which included using a guitar cord allegedly 350 feet long. This allowed him to remain plugged into his amplifier while walking through the crowd and even out into the street during his performances. "Slim was one of the great blues guitarists of the 1950s, and he was also one of the greats showmen, whose performance style included things like a guitar chord that was allegedly 350 feet long."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 32: "I Got A Woman" by Ray Charles

podcast.title: Influence on Jimi Hendrix
podcast.body: Guitar Slim's innovative performance style and guitar work later had a huge influence on musicians like Jimi Hendrix. "Slim would later be a huge influence on musicians like Jimmy Hendrix..."
